card.title: Start the Hard Part
card.instruction: Get someone else to explain, announce, or begin the emotionally difficult part.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you phone Mum and begin the conversation about selling the house?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She asked to speak to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll take over once you've said the word selling.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll put her on speaker. You'll be there for the whole thing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's fine. Introduce the idea, and when she says my full name, I'll answer.

mechanism: A asks B to introduce selling Mum's house before A responds to the emotionally loaded topic.
confusable: Unlike avoiding the whole conversation, A must specifically outsource its difficult beginning.
comparison: D101-b sets a cue for taking over; D101-a sets disappointed silence as the boundary for joining.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
